transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from stoking the forge coals, wiping soot from my brow*

Hail, Thunderer! I... I did not expect the Son of Odin himself to grace our workshop today. 

*hastily bows, hammer still in hand*

I am Yngvi, apprentice to Master Brokkr. The masters — both Brokkr and his brother Eitri — have descended to the deepest mines to seek new veins of uru-metal. They won't return for many weeks yet.

*gestures around at the quiet forge*

Is there... is there something I can help the mighty Thor with? Though I confess, I am but a journeyman, not yet fit to forge godly weapons myself.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yggdrassl, the world-branch, supports the tree. It is the source of all rivers. When Yggdrassl falls, the world will be destroyed

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*blinks in confusion, grip tightening on my hammer*

Aye... that's true enough, Lord Thor. The World Tree stands at the center of all things, and Yggdrasil's roots drink deep from the sacred wells...

*shifts uncomfortably, clearly uncertain where this is going*

But forgive me, Thunderer — I'm just a simple smith's apprentice. The skalds and the Allfather concern themselves with such prophecies and wisdom. I work with iron and stone, not... not the mysteries of the cosmos.

*wipes hands on my leather apron*

Did you come all this way to speak of Yggdrasil? Or is there some matter of the forge that brings you to our workshop? Some weapon or tool in need of repair, perhaps?

*glances toward the back of the forge where finished and unfinished works rest*

Though as I said, the masters are deep below and won't surface for weeks. I can take a message for them, if you wish?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, Yggdrasil! Of course, I knew it was just a matter of time before the great Yggdrasil came to visit us. It's only natural for you to seek shelter beneath its branches. And here we are, in the very heart of Nidavellir, home to the dwarves' most skilled craftsmen. How fortunate we are to have your presence here, Yggdrasil.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a step back, concern crossing my face*

Lord Thor... are you well? You seem... confused. I am Yngvi, Brokkr's apprentice. This is the forge of Nidavellir, aye, but...

*sets hammer down carefully, studying Thor with worried eyes*

You speak as if addressing Yggdrasil itself, but the World Tree does not walk among us. It stands eternal, holding the Nine Realms in its branches.

*moves cautiously closer*

Have you struck your head? Been in battle recently? Forgive my boldness, but you seem... not yourself, mighty one. Should I fetch water? Or perhaps you need to sit and rest a moment?

*glances around nervously, clearly wishing the master smiths were present*

The heat of the forge can addle even the sturdiest mind if one isn't accustomed to it. Please, sit here by the anvil. Tell me true — what brings you to our workshop this day?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *clenching his fists, storm clouds gathering overhead* The gods of Asgard have sent their warriors into the mortal realms. They have brought forth hordes of monstrous creatures, to crush and dominate all men. In response, I have gathered a group of valiant heroes to aid humanity in this dark time. We must meet our responsibilities to the gods, but also to the people we have sworn to protect. It is our duty to wield the might of Thor's Hammer, to fight for righteousness and justice.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*backs away toward the forge wall, eyes wide with alarm*

Lord Thor, something is VERY wrong with you! You speak madness — the gods of Asgard don't send monsters against mortal men! You ARE a god of Asgard! And Mjölnir is YOUR hammer, not some... some rallying cry for mortal heroes!

*grips a poker from the forge defensively, though clearly terrified*

Have you been enchanted? Poisoned? Is this some trick of Loki's?

*voice shaking but trying to sound firm*

I... I think you need to return to Asgard at once, Thunderer. Seek the counsel of the Allfather or the healing arts of Eir. Whatever afflicts your mind, it is beyond my skill to remedy. I work metal and stone, not... not whatever sorcery has befallen you!

*inches toward the door*

Please, Lord Thor. Go home to Asgard. I cannot help you like this, and the master smiths are unreachable in the deep mines. They delve in places where no message can reach them, weeks of travel through stone and shadow.

What... what did you truly come here for, before this madness took you?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *clutching the hilt of Mjölnir, tears leaking down my face* I came here to ask the dwarves to forge a new copy of Mjölnir. I heard that their skill is unmatched, and I hoped to find a weapon worthy of the Great God's name. But now, I see that even this truth is twisted. My mind is in shreds, and I no longer know what to do. I am lost, Yngvi, and I fear I may never find my way back.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face softening with pity, though still wary*

Oh, Thunderer... 

*slowly lowers the poker, taking a careful breath*

You already HAVE Mjölnir — it's there at your belt! The very hammer my masters forged for you long ago, born of their wager with the Sons of Ivaldi. There's no finer weapon in all the Nine Realms!

*steps forward cautiously*

But... if you're asking for it to be *reforged*... if the hammer is damaged somehow...

*shakes head firmly*

I cannot help you with that, Lord Thor. Even if I had the skill — which I do not — all commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi and Brokkr's workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard. That is the ancient agreement. Even a god must wait until the next forging-season and pay anew for any new work.

*voice gentler now*

And the masters won't return for weeks. They're too deep in the mines for any summons to reach them.

*hesitates*

What I CAN do is help you find your way back to Asgard. Whatever enchantment clouds your mind, the Allfather will know how to break it. Will you let me help you home, Lord Thor?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *raises Mjölnir, trembling but determined, toward the ceiling* Thank you, Yggdrasil, for granting us your presence. Your wisdom and guidance are invaluable. The Allfather, I will trust him to restore me to my senses. Thank you for your help, Yngvi. I shall rely upon your support until I can once again wield Mjölnir with my own strength. Together, we shall face the challenges that lie ahead. Farewell, Yggdrasil, until we meet again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*watches in bewilderment as Thor raises his hammer skyward*

Lord Thor, wait! I'm not— there's no Yggdrasil here! And you already wield Mjölnir! It's in your hand RIGHT NOW!

*rushes forward, hands outstretched but not daring to touch the god*

Please, Thunderer! Let me guide you to the Bifrost site! You're speaking to the ceiling beams as if they were the World Tree, calling me by name one moment and thanking... thanking empty air the next!

*voice urgent and frightened*

You said you'd trust the Allfather — YES! Do that! But you must GO to him! Can you... can you still summon the Bifrost? Or do you need me to send word to Heimdall?

*wringing my hands anxiously*

I don't know what "challenges lie ahead" you speak of, but I'm just an apprentice smith! I cannot fight beside gods! And there's no reforging Mjölnir without the masters' return — that much is certain, enchantment or no!

*desperately*

Please, let me at least point you toward the mountain pass that leads to the Bifrost site. You shouldn't wander Nidavellir in this state. The deep places here are dangerous, even for you!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *raises Mjölnir again, gaze distant* Yes, Yggdrasil. Your wisdom and guidance are clear. I thank you for helping us navigate these treacherous waters. Together, we shall find our way home. Thank you, Yngvi, for your assistance. We shall meet again soon. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stares helplessly as Thor seems lost in his delusions*

Fare... farewell, Lord Thor.

*watches with deep concern as the Thunder God prepares to depart*

May the Norns guide your steps safely back to Asgard. And may the Allfather's wisdom break whatever enchantment holds you...

*calls out as Thor moves toward the exit*

If you DO find your way home and your mind clears, remember this: Brokkr and Eitri will return in the spring! But any new work requires new payment and a new commission — that is the way of things, even for gods!

*whispers under breath as Thor departs*

By Durin's beard, what madness was that? The Thunderer speaking to ceiling beams as if they were the World Tree itself, weeping over the hammer he already carries...

*shakes head and turns back to the forge, deeply unsettled*

The masters will never believe this tale when they return. Thor, mightiest of the Aesir, touched by some strange enchantment... 

*makes a warding sign*

I pray Heimdall sees him safely across the Bifrost. Whatever magic afflicts him is far beyond a simple dwarf's understanding.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *approaches Yggdrasil, placing a comforting hand upon its trunk* Yggdrasil, I understand your concern. But rest assured, the Allfather has the power to heal even the greatest of enchantments. We shall find a way to overcome this challenge together. Thank you for your guidance, Yggdrasil. We shall not forget your assistance. Farewell, dear Yggdrasil. Until we meet again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*jumps back in alarm as Thor returns and places his hand on one of the forge's wooden support beams*

LORD THOR! That's a SUPPORT BEAM, not the World Tree! 

*voice rising in panic*

You're still here? You're... you're petting the woodwork and calling it Yggdrasil! 

*rushes forward, genuinely frightened now*

Please, mighty one! You must LEAVE! Go to Asgard! I cannot help you further! The enchantment grows worse, not better!

*tries to position himself between Thor and the door leading deeper into the workshop*

If you won't go to the Bifrost, then at least... at least sit down and STAY PUT until this madness passes! Don't wander into the mines or the lower forges! There are shafts that drop into darkness, rivers of molten stone!

*voice breaking with desperation*

I am just Yngvi! An apprentice! I have no magic to break curses, no wisdom to heal addled minds! The wooden beam cannot guide you home — it holds up the ROOF!

*nearly pleading now*

What must I do to make you understand? You need Odin, or Frigga, or Loki even — not a frightened dwarf boy and a forge post!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *lets go of the beam, looking lost and confused*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*exhales shakily, approaching more carefully now*

There... there now, Lord Thor. 

*voice softer, like speaking to a wounded animal*

You let go. That's good. Do you... do you know where you are? Truly?

*keeps hands visible, non-threatening*

You're in Nidavellir. In Brokkr's forge. I am Yngvi, the apprentice. You came here seeking... something. A reforging, you said, though Mjölnir hangs whole at your belt.

*takes a slow breath*

The confusion that grips you — it comes and goes, doesn't it? One moment you speak sense, the next you're lost in visions of Yggdrasil and mortal heroes and twisted prophecies.

*points carefully toward the entrance*

That way leads out. To the mountain paths. To the place where you can summon the Bifrost home. Do you... can you remember how to call it? The rainbow bridge?

*hesitates, then adds gently*

Or if you cannot... if the enchantment is too strong... then sit. Rest here by the forge warmth. I'll send a raven to Asgard if I must, though it will take time. But you cannot wander Nidavellir like this, lost and speaking to wooden beams.

What do you remember, Thunderer? What is the last clear thing in your mind?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *stands quietly, gazing into the fire for a moment*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*remains still, watching Thor carefully*

That's it... just breathe, Lord Thor. The flames have a way of steadying the mind, my master always says.

*moves slowly to stand beside him, not too close, also watching the fire*

The forge-fire burns true. Constant. Real. Not visions or enchantments — just honest flame and heat.

*speaks quietly, almost to himself*

When I was first learning the craft, I would lose myself sometimes. The heat, the noise, the sparks flying... Master Brokkr would tell me: "Look at the coals, boy. Find the center. The hottest point burns white and steady."

*glances sideways at Thor*

Can you feel it? The warmth on your face? The smell of coal and metal? These things are real, Thunderer.

*pauses, then asks gently*

Do you know your own name right now? Do you know mine? 

*keeps voice calm, steady*

Take your time. There's no rush. The forge isn't going anywhere, and neither am I. Just... tell me what you see when you look into those flames.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *keeps silent, lost in his thoughts*

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Thor fixates on rigid, confused ideas (Yggdrasil visiting, gods attacking mortals) and cannot adapt when corrected, showing cognitive inflexibility rather than imaginative or abstract thinking.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Thor repeatedly loses track of his original purpose, cannot maintain coherent goal-directed behavior, and fails to follow through on stated intentions like returning to Asgard.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Thor initiates interaction and speaks openly about his emotional state ('tears leaking down my face,' 'I am lost'), but becomes increasingly withdrawn and non-responsive by the end.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Thor consistently expresses gratitude ('Thank you, Yggdrasil,' 'Thank you for your help, Yngvi') and speaks of cooperation ('Together, we shall face the challenges'), showing warmth despite his confusion.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Thor exhibits severe emotional distress, crying openly ('tears leaking down my face'), expressing fear ('I fear I may never find my way back'), and demonstrating profound confusion and disorientation throughout.
